func (p *commitPipeline) prepare(b *Batch, syncWAL bool, noSyncWait bool) (*memTable, error) {
	n := uint64(b.Count())
	if n == invalidBatchCount {
		return nil, ErrInvalidBatch
	}
	var syncWG *sync.WaitGroup
	var syncErr *error
	switch {
	case !syncWAL:
		// Only need to wait for the publish.
		b.commit.Add(1)
	// Remaining cases represent syncWAL=true.
	case noSyncWait:
		syncErr = &b.commitErr
		syncWG = &b.fsyncWait
		// Only need to wait synchronously for the publish. The user will
		// (asynchronously) wait on the batch's fsyncWait.
		b.commit.Add(1)
		b.fsyncWait.Add(1)
	case !noSyncWait:
		syncErr = &b.commitErr
		syncWG = &b.commit
		// Must wait for both the publish and the WAL fsync.
		b.commit.Add(2)
	}

	p.mu.Lock()

	// Enqueue the batch in the pending queue. Note that while the pending queue
	// is lock-free, we want the order of batches to be the same as the sequence
	// number order.
	p.pending.enqueue(b)

	// Assign the batch a sequence number. Note that we use atomic operations
	// here to handle concurrent reads of logSeqNum. commitPipeline.mu provides
	// mutual exclusion for other goroutines writing to logSeqNum.
	b.setSeqNum(p.env.logSeqNum.Add(base.SeqNum(n)) - base.SeqNum(n))

	// Write the data to the WAL.
	mem, err := p.env.write(b, syncWG, syncErr)

	p.mu.Unlock()

	return mem, err
}

func (p *commitPipeline) publish(b *Batch) {
	// Mark the batch as applied.
	b.applied.Store(true)

	// Loop dequeuing applied batches from the pending queue. If our batch was
	// the head of the pending queue we are guaranteed that either we'll publish
	// it or someone else will dequeueApplied and publish it. If our batch is not the
	// head of the queue then either we'll dequeueApplied applied batches and reach our
	// batch or there is an unapplied batch blocking us. When that unapplied
	// batch applies it will go through the same process and publish our batch
	// for us.
	for {
		t := p.pending.dequeueApplied()
		if t == nil {
			// Wait for another goroutine to publish us. We might also be waiting for
			// the WAL sync to finish.
			now := crtime.NowMono()
			b.commit.Wait()
			b.commitStats.CommitWaitDuration += now.Elapsed()
			break
		}
		if !t.applied.Load() {
			panic("not reached")
		}

		// We're responsible for publishing the sequence number for batch t, but
		// another concurrent goroutine might sneak in and publish the sequence
		// number for a subsequent batch. That's ok as all we're guaranteeing is
		// that the sequence number ratchets up.
		for {
			curSeqNum := p.env.visibleSeqNum.Load()
			newSeqNum := t.SeqNum() + base.SeqNum(t.Count())
			if newSeqNum <= curSeqNum {
				// t's sequence number has already been published.
				break
			}
			if p.env.visibleSeqNum.CompareAndSwap(curSeqNum, newSeqNum) {
				// We successfully published t's sequence number.
				break
			}
		}

		t.commit.Done()
	}
}
	}
	return uint32(b.count)
}

// Reader returns a batchrepr.Reader for the current batch contents. If the
// batch is mutated, the new entries will not be visible to the reader.
func (b *Batch) Reader() batchrepr.Reader {
	if len(b.data) == 0 {
		b.init(batchrepr.HeaderLen)
	}
	return batchrepr.Read(b.data)
}

// SyncWait is to be used in conjunction with DB.ApplyNoSyncWait.
func (b *Batch) SyncWait() error {
	now := crtime.NowMono()
	b.fsyncWait.Wait()
	if b.commitErr != nil {
		b.db = nil // prevent batch reuse on error
	}
	waitDuration := now.Elapsed()
	b.commitStats.CommitWaitDuration += waitDuration
	b.commitStats.TotalDuration += waitDuration
	return b.commitErr
}

// CommitStats returns stats related to committing the batch. Should be called
// after Batch.Commit, DB.Apply. If DB.ApplyNoSyncWait is used, should be
// called after Batch.SyncWait.
func (b *Batch) CommitStats() BatchCommitStats {
	return b.commitStats
}

// Note: batchIter mirrors the implementation of flushableBatchIter. Keep the
// two in sync.
type batchIter struct {
// batch commits. The caller can use these stats to do their own tracing as
// needed.
type BatchCommitStats struct {
	// TotalDuration is the time spent in DB.{Apply,ApplyNoSyncWait} or
	// Batch.Commit, plus the time waiting in Batch.SyncWait. If there is a gap
	// between calling ApplyNoSyncWait and calling SyncWait, that gap could
	// include some duration in which real work was being done for the commit
	// and will not be included here. This missing time is considered acceptable
	// since the goal of these stats is to understand user-facing latency.
	//
	// TotalDuration includes time spent in various queues both inside Pebble
	// and outside Pebble (I/O queues, goroutine scheduler queue, mutex wait
	// etc.). For some of these queues (which we consider important) the wait
	// times are included below -- these expose low-level implementation detail
	// and are meant for expert diagnosis and subject to change. There may be
	// unaccounted time after subtracting those values from TotalDuration.
	TotalDuration time.Duration
	// SemaphoreWaitDuration is the wait time for semaphores in
	// commitPipeline.Commit.
	SemaphoreWaitDuration time.Duration
	// WALQueueWaitDuration is the wait time for allocating memory blocks in the
	// LogWriter (due to the LogWriter not writing fast enough). At the moment
	// this is duration is always zero because a single WAL will allow
	// allocating memory blocks up to the entire memtable size. In the future,
	// we may pipeline WALs and bound the WAL queued blocks separately, so this
	// field is preserved for that possibility.
	WALQueueWaitDuration time.Duration
	// MemTableWriteStallDuration is the wait caused by a write stall due to too
	// many memtables (due to not flushing fast enough).
	MemTableWriteStallDuration time.Duration
	// L0ReadAmpWriteStallDuration is the wait caused by a write stall due to
	// high read amplification in L0 (due to not compacting fast enough out of
	// L0).
	L0ReadAmpWriteStallDuration time.Duration
	// WALRotationDuration is the wait time for WAL rotation, which includes
	// syncing and closing the old WAL and creating (or reusing) a new one.
	WALRotationDuration time.Duration
	// CommitWaitDuration is the wait for publishing the seqnum plus the
	// duration for the WAL sync (if requested). The former should be tiny and
	// one can assume that this is all due to the WAL sync.
	CommitWaitDuration time.Duration
}

package pebble

import (
	"context"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/cockroachdb/errors"
	"github.com/cockroachdb/pebble/internal/base"
	"github.com/cockroachdb/pebble/vfs"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

type batchDurableRecorder struct {
	mu    sync.Mutex
	infos []BatchDurableInfo
}

func (r *batchDurableRecorder) record(info BatchDurableInfo) {
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	r.infos = append(r.infos, info)
}

func (r *batchDurableRecorder) get() []BatchDurableInfo {
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	return append([]BatchDurableInfo(nil), r.infos...)
}

func openDurabilityTestDB(t *testing.T, r *batchDurableRecorder, disableWAL bool) *DB {
	opts := &Options{FS: vfs.NewMem(), DisableWAL: disableWAL}
	if r != nil {
		opts.EventListener = &EventListener{BatchDurable: r.record}
	}
	d, err := Open("", opts)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	return d
}

func TestBatchDurableEvent(t *testing.T) {
	var r batchDurableRecorder
	d := openDurabilityTestDB(t, &r, false)
	defer func() { require.NoError(t, d.Close()) }()

	// Zero values before any commits.
	require.Equal(t, DurabilityStats{}, d.DurabilityStats())
	seq, err := d.DurableState()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Zero(t, seq)
	require.NoError(t, d.WaitForDurability(0))

	// Non-sync commits never fire.
	require.NoError(t, d.Set([]byte("a"), []byte("1"), NoSync))
	require.Empty(t, r.get())

	b := d.NewBatch()
	require.NoError(t, b.Set([]byte("b"), []byte("2"), nil))
	require.NoError(t, b.Set([]byte("c"), []byte("3"), nil))
	size := len(b.Repr())
	require.NoError(t, b.Commit(&WriteOptions{Sync: true, CommitCorrelationID: 42}))
	infos := r.get()
	require.Len(t, infos, 1)
	info := infos[0]
	require.NoError(t, info.Err)
	require.Equal(t, b.SeqNum(), info.SeqNum)
	require.Equal(t, uint64(42), info.CorrelationID)
	require.Equal(t, size, info.BatchSize)
	require.Equal(t, uint32(2), info.KeyCount)
	require.Positive(t, info.ApplyDuration)
	require.Positive(t, info.SyncDuration)
	require.Positive(t, info.JobID)
	require.NoError(t, b.Close())

	require.NoError(t, d.WaitForDurability(info.SeqNum+1))
	require.NoError(t, d.WaitForDurabilityBatch([]base.SeqNum{1, info.SeqNum}))
	require.NoError(t, d.WaitForDurabilityBatch(nil))
	require.NoError(t, d.WaitForJobDurability(info.JobID))
	require.NoError(t, <-d.DurabilityNotify(info.SeqNum))
	seq, err = d.DurableState()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, info.SeqNum+1, seq)

	// ApplyNoSyncWait reports from SyncWait.
	b = d.NewBatch()
	require.NoError(t, b.Set([]byte("d"), []byte("4"), nil))
	require.NoError(t, d.ApplyNoSyncWait(b, Sync))
	require.NoError(t, b.SyncWait())
	require.Len(t, r.get(), 2)
	require.Equal(t, b.SeqNum(), r.get()[1].SeqNum)
	require.NoError(t, b.Close())

	stats := d.DurabilityStats()
	require.Equal(t, uint64(2), stats.TotalDurableCommits)
	require.Zero(t, stats.TotalFailedCommits)
	require.Positive(t, stats.CumulativeSyncDuration)
	require.Positive(t, stats.MaxSyncDuration)
	require.Zero(t, stats.PendingWaiters)

	m := d.Metrics()
	require.Equal(t, uint64(2), m.DurableCommitCount)
	require.Equal(t, stats.CumulativeSyncDuration, m.DurableCommitDuration)
}

func TestDurabilityWaitersAndClose(t *testing.T) {
	d := openDurabilityTestDB(t, nil, false)

	require.Error(t, d.WaitForJobDurability(0))
	require.Contains(t, d.WaitForJobDurability(0).Error(), "unknown")
	require.Contains(t, d.WaitForJobDurability(7).Error(), "unknown")

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Millisecond)
	defer cancel()
	require.ErrorIs(t, d.WaitForDurabilityContext(ctx, 1000), context.DeadlineExceeded)

	// Durability is tracked without a configured listener, but metrics are not.
	for i := 0; i < durabilityJobRetention+10; i++ {
		require.NoError(t, d.Set([]byte("a"), []byte("1"), Sync))
	}
	require.Contains(t, d.WaitForJobDurability(1).Error(), "expired")
	require.Zero(t, d.Metrics().DurableCommitCount)
	require.Equal(t, uint64(durabilityJobRetention+10), d.DurabilityStats().TotalDurableCommits)

	seq, _ := d.DurableState()
	notifyCh := d.DurabilityNotify(seq + 100)
	errCh := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() { errCh <- d.WaitForDurability(seq + 100) }()
	require.Eventually(t, func() bool { return d.DurabilityStats().PendingWaiters == 1 },
		10*time.Second, time.Millisecond)

	// Exceeding the subscription bound yields an immediate error.
	var chans []<-chan error
	for i := 0; i < maxDurabilitySubscriptions; i++ {
		chans = append(chans, d.DurabilityNotify(seq+200))
	}
	require.ErrorIs(t, <-chans[len(chans)-1], ErrTooManyDurabilitySubscriptions)

	require.NoError(t, d.Close())
	require.ErrorIs(t, <-errCh, ErrClosed)
	require.ErrorIs(t, <-notifyCh, ErrClosed)
	require.ErrorIs(t, <-chans[0], ErrClosed)
	require.Zero(t, d.DurabilityStats().PendingWaiters)
}

func TestDurabilityDisableWAL(t *testing.T) {
	var r batchDurableRecorder
	d := openDurabilityTestDB(t, &r, true)
	defer func() { require.NoError(t, d.Close()) }()
	require.NoError(t, d.Set([]byte("a"), []byte("1"), NoSync))
	require.Error(t, d.Set([]byte("a"), []byte("1"), Sync))
	require.Empty(t, r.get())
	require.NoError(t, d.WaitForDurability(1000))
	require.NoError(t, d.WaitForDurabilityBatch([]base.SeqNum{1000}))
	require.NoError(t, d.WaitForJobDurability(5))
	require.NoError(t, <-d.DurabilityNotify(1000))
}

func TestDurabilityFailure(t *testing.T) {
	var tr durabilityTracker
	ch := tr.notify(10)
	_, w := tr.record(1, 1, nil, time.Millisecond, false)
	w.release()
	syncErr := errors.New("sync failed")
	job, w := tr.record(2, 1, syncErr, 0, false)
	w.release()
	require.ErrorIs(t, <-ch, syncErr)
	require.ErrorIs(t, tr.waitJob(job), syncErr)
	require.NoError(t, tr.wait(context.Background(), 1))
	require.ErrorIs(t, tr.wait(context.Background(), 2), syncErr)
	seq, err := tr.state()
	require.Equal(t, base.SeqNum(1), seq)
	require.ErrorIs(t, err, syncErr)
	s := tr.stats()
	require.Equal(t, uint64(1), s.TotalDurableCommits)
	require.Equal(t, uint64(1), s.TotalFailedCommits)
}

func TestTeeEventListenerBatchDurable(t *testing.T) {
	require.True(t, isNoopBatchDurable(TeeEventListener(EventListener{}, EventListener{}).BatchDurable))
	var a, b batchDurableRecorder
	l := TeeEventListener(EventListener{BatchDurable: a.record}, EventListener{BatchDurable: b.record})
	l.BatchDurable(BatchDurableInfo{JobID: 1})
	require.Len(t, a.get(), 1)
	require.Len(t, b.get(), 1)
}

db: add BatchDurable event and durability wait APIs

Previously, EventListener reported flushes, compactions and other
background events, but nothing reported when a committed batch became
durable. Callers that need to know a sync write has hit disk before
acking clients or propagating to replicas had no hook for it.

This change adds EventListener.BatchDurable, which fires exactly once
per Sync commit after the WAL sync completes, including on failure. For
DB.ApplyNoSyncWait the event fires from Batch.SyncWait. Non-sync commits
and DisableWAL never trigger it. BatchDurableInfo carries a job ID, the
batch seqnum, error, apply and sync durations, the new
WriteOptions.CommitCorrelationID, the encoded batch size and key count.

Every DB now tracks the highest durable seqnum established by sync
commits in a durabilityTracker, and exposes WaitForDurability,
WaitForDurabilityBatch and WaitForJobDurability (plus Context variants),
DurableState, DurabilityNotify and DurabilityStats. Job outcomes are
retained for a bounded window, with distinct "expired" and "unknown"
errors outside it, and DurabilityNotify subscriptions are bounded.
Waiters are released with an error on WAL sync failure or DB close, and
the wait APIs return nil immediately when the WAL is disabled. Waiters
are released after the listener is invoked, so the callback has run by
the time a blocked waiter returns.

EnsureDefaults installs a named no-op BatchDurable so the DB can still
tell whether a callback was configured; TeeEventListener preserves this.
Metrics.DurableCommitCount and DurableCommitDuration (cumulative WAL
sync phase time) are maintained only when BatchDurable is configured.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

content.text:
I added the `BatchDurable` event and the durability APIs, and committed them as `83c3f719` on a new branch, `batch-durable-listener`. This repo has no `main` branch, so I branched from `master` (at `1454d2bc`). The root package tests and lint pass with `-tags invariants`; the new tests also pass under `-race`. `go vet ./...` and the `tool`, `cmd`, `wal` and `record` tests are clean. I didn't run the full `./...` suite.

**How it works**
- **When the callback fires:** for `Apply`/`Batch.Commit` with Sync, it fires just before the call returns. If the commit fails, it fires with the error before the existing `Fatalf`. For `ApplyNoSyncWait`, it fires from `Batch.SyncWait`, which is when the sync is actually observed. Empty batches, non-sync commits and the DisableWAL path never fire it.
- **Durable sequence number:** a successful sync commit marks everything up to the batch's last sequence number as durable, not just its first. That includes earlier non-sync writes, since a WAL sync covers everything written before it. Only sync commits move this number, so a non-sync write isn't counted as durable until a later sync commit.
- **Order of events:** the state is updated first, then the callback runs, then blocked waiters are released. A waiter that wakes up can rely on the callback having already run, and calling `WaitForDurability(info.SeqNum)` from inside the callback won't deadlock.
- **Errors:** the first failure is kept. After that, any wait for a sequence number that isn't already durable returns that error. Closing the DB releases blocked waiters and open notify channels with `ErrClosed`. Durability and close errors are checked before the context's error.
- **Bounds:** the job-ID retention window and the `DurabilityNotify` subscription cap are both 1024. The "expired", "unknown" and "too many subscriptions" errors are exported so callers can check for them.
- **Detecting a configured callback:** `EnsureDefaults` installs a named no-op for `BatchDurable`, so every field stays non-nil (an existing test requires that) and the DB can still tell whether a real callback was set. `TeeEventListener` keeps the no-op if neither side sets one.

**Choices you may want to revisit**
- **Job IDs** come from their own counter, separate from the job IDs used by flush and compaction events. A shared counter would mean taking `d.mu` on every sync commit.
- **`WaitForJobDurability` never blocks.** A job ID only exists once its sync has finished, so the call just returns that job's result.
- **`SyncDuration`** runs from when the WAL write is queued until the sync completes, so it overlaps the memtable apply. For `ApplyNoSyncWait`, it also includes any delay before the caller reaches `SyncWait`. Both durations are rounded up to at least 1ns on success, so they're always positive.
- **Counters** (`DurableCommitCount`, `DurableCommitDuration`, `CumulativeSyncDuration`, `MaxSyncDuration`) count only successful commits. Failures appear only in `TotalFailedCommits`.
- **`MakeLoggingEventListener`** logs `BatchDurable` only when it fails. Logging every sync commit would be very noisy and would likely break existing test output.
- **When the WAL is disabled,** `WaitForJobDurability` returns nil even for zero or never-seen IDs, because the spec says the wait APIs return nil immediately in that mode.

The new code is in `durability.go`, with tests in `durability_test.go`.

**How it works**
- **When the callback fires:** for `Apply`/`Batch.Commit` with Sync, it fires just before the call returns. If the commit fails, it fires with the error before the existing `Fatalf`. For `ApplyNoSyncWait`, it fires from `Batch.SyncWait`, which is when the sync is actually observed. Empty batches, non-sync commits and the DisableWAL path never fire it.
- **Durable sequence number:** a successful sync commit marks everything up to the batch's last sequence number as durable, not just its first. That includes earlier non-sync writes, since a WAL sync covers everything written before it. Only sync commits move this number, so a non-sync write isn't counted as durable until a later sync commit.
- **Order of events:** the state is updated first, then the callback runs, then blocked waiters are released. A waiter that wakes up can rely on the callback having already run, and calling `WaitForDurability(info.SeqNum)` from inside the callback won't deadlock.
- **Errors:** the first failure is kept. After that, any wait for a sequence number that isn't already durable returns that error. Closing the DB releases blocked waiters and open notify channels with `ErrClosed`. Durability and close errors are checked before the context's error.
- **Bounds:** the job-ID retention window and the `DurabilityNotify` subscription cap are both 1024. The "expired", "unknown" and "too many subscriptions" errors are exported so callers can check for them.
- **Detecting a configured callback:** `EnsureDefaults` installs a named no-op for `BatchDurable`, so every field stays non-nil (an existing test requires that) and the DB can still tell whether a real callback was set. `TeeEventListener` keeps the no-op if neither side sets one.

**Choices you may want to revisit**
- **Job IDs** come from their own counter, separate from the job IDs used by flush and compaction events. A shared counter would mean taking `d.mu` on every sync commit.
- **`WaitForJobDurability` never blocks.** A job ID only exists once its sync has finished, so the call just returns that job's result.

- **Counters** (`DurableCommitCount`, `DurableCommitDuration`, `CumulativeSyncDuration`, `MaxSyncDuration`) count only successful commits. Failures appear only in `TotalFailedCommits`.
- **`MakeLoggingEventListener`** logs `BatchDurable` only when it fails. Logging every sync commit would be very noisy and would likely break existing test output.
- **When the WAL is disabled,** `WaitForJobDurability` returns nil even for zero or never-seen IDs, because the spec says the wait APIs return nil immediately in that mode.

The new code is in `durability.go`, with tests in `durability_test.go`.
